Rashi on Megillah 8a:10:1.hebrew: משכב ומושב - שכב או ישב על גבי עשרה בגדים זה על זה, כולן אבות הטומאה, ואפילו לא נגע בהן; ואילו נגע בדבר שאינו משכב ומושב, אינו [אלא] ראשון לטומאה, ואינו מטמא אדם וכלים, אלא אוכלין ומשקין:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:10:1.english: Lying and sitting - [If he] lay or sat upon ten garments, one on top of another, they are all primary sources of ritual impurity, even if he did not touch them [directly]; whereas if he touched something that is not [designated for] lying or sitting, it is [only] a first-degree [source of] ritual impurity, and it does not render people or vessels impure, only food and drink:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:10:2.hebrew: וספירת שבעה - משיפסוק, צריך למנות ז' נקיים קודם שיטבול, ואם ראה זוב באחד מהן, סתר כל המנויין:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:10:2.english: And the counting of seven - Once [the discharge] stops, he must count seven clean [days] before he immerses, and if he saw a zov [emission] on one of them, he forfeits all the [days] counted:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:11:1.english: From where are these matters [derived] - That they are equal with respect to impurity, yet are not equal with respect to an offering:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:11:2.hebrew: מנה הכתוב שתים - "ואיש כי יהיה זב מבשרו זובו טמא הוא" (ויקרא ט״ו:ב׳) — הרי שתי זיבות מנויות כאן, וקראו "טמא":
Rashi on Megillah 8a:11:2.english: The verse enumerated two - "When any man has an emission out of his flesh, due to his emission he is impure" (Leviticus 15:2) — here two emissions are enumerated, and it called him "impure":

Rashi on Megillah 8a:11:3.hebrew: שלש וקראו טמא - דכתיב: "וזאת תהיה טומאתו בזובו, רר בשרו את זובו או החתים בשרו מזובו" (שם) — הרי לך שלש; וקראו טמא: "טומאתו היא":
Rashi on Megillah 8a:11:3.english: Three [emissions], and it called him impure - As it is written: "And this shall be his impurity in his emission: whether his flesh runs with his emission, or his flesh be stopped from his emission" (ibid.) — here you have three [mentions of emission]; and it called him impure: "it is his impurity":

Rashi on Megillah 8a:11:4.hebrew: הא כיצד - אם משתים טמא, למה פרט לך הכתוב שלש:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:11:4.english: How so - If from two [emissions] he is impure, why did Scripture specify three for you?

Rashi on Megillah 8a:12:1.english: Two [emissions] to [establish] impurity - for every stringency of the impurity of a zav:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:12:2.hebrew: ולא לטומאה - חמורה, אלא כבעל קרי בעלמא:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:12:2.english: And not for impurity - [i.e.,] severe [impurity], rather [he is impure] merely like an ordinary ba'al keri [one who experienced a seminal emission]:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:12:3.hebrew: ראה שתים - והרי כבר ירד לכל חומר טומאה, ומי הוציאו:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:12:3.english: He experienced two - And behold, he has already entered into the full stringency of impurity, so who removed him [from it]?

Rashi on Megillah 8a:13:1.english: From his emission - [This] implies part of his emission:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:15:1.hebrew: לא ידענא כמה ראיות - האי "מקצת" דמשמע מהאי קרא, לא ידעינן מאי היא: או שלש וארבע, או שתים ושלש:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:15:1.english: I would not have known how many emissions - This "part" [i.e., partial inclusion] that is implied by this verse ["from his emission"], we do not know what it is: whether [it means] three [emissions for impurity] and four [for an offering], or two [for impurity] and three [for an offering]:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:17:1.hebrew: לכשיפסוק מזובו - אין צריך ליטבול קודם ספירה, אלא משיפסוק ימנה. הכי גרסינן בתורת כהנים: "מזובו" — ולא מזובו ומנגעו; שאם היה זב ומצורע, ופסק מזובו ולא נתרפא עדיין מנגעו, וספר — אין אומרים לו: "אין ספירה זו נקיות עד שיטהר אף מנגעו", אלא מונה והולך מיד, ועולה לו לספירת זוב. ולכשיתרפא מצרעתו, יטבול מיד טבילה ראשונה של מצורע, והיא עולה לו לטבילת נגעו וזובו, ונטהר מלטמא משכב ומושב ולטמא כלי חרס בהיסט כדין זב. ואף על פי שצריך לספירת שבעה לצרעתו לענין אכילת קדשים וטבילה שניה — כדכתיב במצורע (ויקרא י״ד:ח׳-ט׳): "ורחץ במים וטהר ואחר יבא אל המחנה וישב מחוץ לאהלו שבעת ימים והיה ביום השביעי יגלח את כל שערו וגו' ורחץ בשרו במים וגו'" — אהני טבילה קמייתא לטהרו מלטמא משכב ומושב וכלי חרס בהיסט:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:17:1.english: When he ceases from his emission - He does not need to immerse before counting [the seven clean days]; rather, once [his emission] ceases, he counts. This is how we read [the text] in Torat Kohanim: "From his emission" — and not from his emission and his affliction; for if he was [both] a zav and a metzora, and he ceased from his emission while not yet healed from his affliction, and he counted [the seven days] — we do not say to him, "This count is not [one of] cleanness until he is purified from his affliction as well"; rather, he continues counting immediately and it counts for him toward the counting of [his] zav [status]. And when he is healed from his tzara'at, he immerses immediately [with] the first immersion of a metzora, and it counts for him for the immersion of [both] his affliction and his emission, and he becomes purified from rendering a couch or seat impure, and from rendering an earthenware vessel impure through moving [it], as is the law of a zav. And even though he [still] requires a count of seven [days] for his tzara'at with respect to eating consecrated [foods] and a second immersion — as it is written regarding a metzora (Leviticus 14:8-9): "And he shall wash in water and be pure, and afterward he shall come into the camp, and he shall dwell outside his tent seven days. And it shall be on the seventh day, he shall shave all his hair, etc., and he shall wash his flesh in water, etc." — the first immersion is effective to purify him from rendering a couch or seat impure, and [from rendering] an earthenware vessel impure through moving [it]:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:17:2.hebrew: מזובו וספר - להכי סמך ספירה אצל זובו, ללמדך שאף בשביל מקצת זב טעון ספירה; "לימד על זב בעל שתי ראיות":
Rashi on Megillah 8a:17:2.english: From his emission, then he shall count - For this reason [Scripture] juxtaposed counting next to "his emission" [indicating "part of"], to teach you that even on account of part of [a full] emission [of a zav], he requires counting [seven clean days]; [thus the baraita states:] "This teaches concerning a zav who experienced two emissions":

Rashi on Megillah 8a:18:1.hebrew: לא יהא טעון ספירת שבעה - בתמיה, אחר שאמרת שתים כו'; וה"ג: הלא דין הוא, אם מטמא משכב ומושב בשתי ראיות לכל חומר טומאת זב, מהיכן יתמעט מספירה:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:18:1.english: Would he not require a count of seven - [This is said] in astonishment: after you have said two [emissions], etc. And this is the [correct] reading: Is it not logical — if he renders [a surface for] lying and sitting ritually impure through two sightings [of discharge], [subjecting him] to all the stringency of the impurity of a zav, from where would he be excluded from counting [seven clean days]?

Rashi on Megillah 8a:1:1.english: There is no [difference] between one who is forbidden by a vow [from deriving] benefit - [One who is] forbidden by a vow [from deriving] benefit is more stringent than [one who is] forbidden by a vow [from] food:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:1:2.hebrew: דריסת הרגל - שהמודר הנאה אסור ליכנס לביתו, והמודר מאכל מותר:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:1:2.english: Stepping foot - For one who is prohibited by a vow from [deriving] benefit is forbidden to enter his house, whereas one who is prohibited by a vow from [his] food is permitted [to do so]:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:1:3.hebrew: וכלים שאין עושין בהן אוכל נפש - מותר להשאיל למודר מאכל, ודוקא במקום שאין משכירין כיוצא בהן; אבל במקום שמשכירין כיוצא בהן, תנן בהדיא דאסור, דכל הנאה שאם לא ההנהו זה היה מחסר בה פרוטה — הנאת מאכל היא, שהרי ראויה אותה פרוטה לקנות בה מאכל:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:1:3.english: And utensils with which one does not prepare food - [These] may be lent to one who is prohibited by vow from [another's] food, specifically in a place where [utensils] like them are not rented out; however, in a place where [utensils] like them are rented out, we have learned explicitly that it is forbidden, because any benefit where, had this [person] not provided him the benefit, he would have lost a perutah on it — is [considered] a food benefit, since that perutah is fit to buy food with:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:2:1.hebrew: הא לענין כלים שעושין בהן אוכל נפש - אסור אף במודר מאכל, ואפי' במקום שאין משכירים:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:2:1.english: [This implies] that with regard to utensils with which food is prepared - it is prohibited even for one who is under a vow [not to benefit] from food, and even in a place where they do not rent [them] out:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:3:1.english: Why, people are not particular - and why is it prohibited for one who is forbidden by a vow from deriving benefit?

Rashi on Megillah 8a:3:2.english: Overlooking - something that one would concede to any person and is not particular about:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:4:1.hebrew: נדר ונדבה - מפרש בגמרא: נדר — האומר "הרי עלי עולה", ולאחר זמן הפרישה, חייב באחריותה; נדבה — האומר "הרי זו", ולא קבלה עליו:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:4:1.english: Vow and gift [offerings] - [This is] explained in the Gemara: a vow [offering is] one who says, "It is hereby [incumbent] upon me [to bring] a burnt offering," and after a time designates it — he is obligated in its responsibility; a gift [offering is] one who says, "This [animal] is hereby [consecrated]," and he did not accept it upon himself:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:5:1.hebrew: הא לענין בל תאחר - ואף על גב דנדבה בקרא דבל תאחר לא כתיבא, הא מרבינן ליה במסכת ראש השנה מגזרה שוה:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:5:1.english: But regarding [the prohibition of] "do not delay" - And even though a gift offering is not written in the verse of "do not delay," we nevertheless include it in Tractate Rosh Hashanah through a gezerah shavah [verbal analogy].

Rashi on Megillah 8a:7:1.hebrew: את שעליו חייב באחריותו - הכי דרש ליה לקרא: "ונרצה לו" נדרו — לכשיתכפר בהן הויא נרצה, אבל מקמי כפרה לא נרצה; ובאיזה קרבן אמרתי לך? באותו שעליו, והיינו "עליו" דקרא:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:7:1.english: That which is [incumbent] upon him, he bears responsibility [to replace] it - This is how he expounds the verse: "And it shall be accepted for him" — his vow [is accepted] when atonement is effected through it, [then] it is accepted, but prior to atonement it is not accepted. And regarding which offering did I say [this] to you? Regarding that [offering] which is [incumbent] upon him; and that is [the meaning of] "upon him" in the verse:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:8:1.english: From where is it inferred - that [the word] "upon him" [indicates] accepting responsibility upon himself:

Rashi on Megillah 8a:9:1.hebrew: שתי ראיות - ביום אחד או בשני ימים רצופים, וכן שלש: ביום אחד, או בשלשה ימים רצופין, או שתים ביום אחד ואחת למחר:
Rashi on Megillah 8a:9:1.english: Two emissions - on one day or on two consecutive days; and similarly, three [emissions]: on one day, or on three consecutive days, or two on one day and one on the following day:

Tosafot on Megillah 8a:18:1.hebrew: יש ספרים דגרסי ומה מצורע שאין מטמא משכב ומושב - ובתורת כהנים תני שמטמא משכב ומושב, ותירץ רש"י בפסחים (דף סז: ד"ה זב) דהיינו לטמא אוכלין ומשקין, אבל לא לטמא אדם וכלים, כגון זב:
Tosafot on Megillah 8a:18:1.english: There are texts that read: "And just as a metzora, who does not render a surface for lying and sitting impure" - Yet in Torat Kohanim it is taught that [a metzora] does render a surface for lying and sitting impure! And Rashi in Pesachim (67b, s.v. zav) resolved [this]: that [teaching] refers to rendering food and drink impure, but not to rendering people and vessels impure, like a zav:

Tosafot on Megillah 8a:1:1.hebrew: אלא דריסת הרגל וכלים שאין עושין בהן אוכל נפש - דמודר הנאה אסור בהן, ומודר מאכל מותר במקום שאין משכירין. אבל במקום שמשכירין בפרוטה, אסור אפי' במודר מאכל, דאותה פרוטה ראויה לקנות ממנה מאכל; אבל כלים שעושין בהן אוכל נפש, אסור אפילו בפחות משוה פרוטה, כיון דהוי אוכל נפש:
Tosafot on Megillah 8a:1:1.english: Except for stepping foot and utensils with which one does not prepare food - For one who is forbidden by vow from [deriving] benefit is prohibited from them, whereas one who is forbidden by vow from food is permitted [to use them] in a place where they do not rent [them out]. However, in a place where they rent [them out] for a peruta, it is prohibited even for one who is forbidden by vow from food, because that peruta is fit to buy food with it; whereas utensils with which one prepares food are prohibited even for less than the value of a peruta, since it is [for] food preparation:

Tosafot on Megillah 8a:3:1.hebrew: דריסת הרגל הא לא קפדי אינשי - קשה, דהא בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף נז:) קאמר בגמרא: אלו דברים שאין להם חזקה ואלו דברים שיש להם חזקה וכו', מעמיד בהמה בחצר אין להם חזקה; ומוקי לה התם בשותפין, דבהעמדה כדי לא קפדי. ופריך: והתנן השותפין שנדרו הנאה זה מזה אסורין ליכנס בחצר! ומשני לה התם. מיהו שמעינן לה מינה דאדריסת הרגל קפדי! ולא קשה מההיא דהתם פרק בתרא דביצה (דף לט:), דמשני התם דלעולם לא קפדי ומני ר' אליעזר היא — דלמא התם מיירי בשותפין, אבל שאר אינשי ודאי קפדי; אבל הכא קשיא, דמיירי בסתם בני אדם, ואפי' הכי קאמר דלא קפדי! ותירץ ר"ת, דהכא מיירי בבקעה דלא קפדי בה שום אדם; וסברא הוא לומר כן, דומיא (דרישא) דכלים שאין עושין בהן אוכל נפש, דמיירי שאין משכירין כיוצא בהן, דמוקימנן לה בנדרים (דף לב:) כרבי אליעזר:
Tosafot on Megillah 8a:3:1.english: Stepping foot; aren’t people not particular? - This is difficult, for in [the chapter entitled] Chezkas HaBattim (Bava Batra 57b) the Gemara says: "These are the things that do not have chazakah, and these are the things that have chazakah, etc. — one who stations an animal in a courtyard does not have chazakah [over it]." And [the Gemara] establishes it there [as referring] to partners, who are not particular about such stationing. And it asks: "But did we not learn [in a Mishnah]: Partners who vowed [not to derive] benefit from one another are forbidden to enter the courtyard?" And it answers it there. However, we learn from this that regarding stepping foot, [people] are particular! And there is no difficulty from that [passage] there in the last chapter of Beitzah (39b), where [the Gemara] answers that in fact they are not particular and whose [opinion] is it? It is Rabbi Eliezer — [for] perhaps there it is speaking of partners, whereas other people are certainly particular; but here it is difficult, since it is speaking of ordinary people, and even so it says that they are not particular! And Rabbeinu Tam answered that here it is speaking of an open field, regarding which no person is particular; and it is logical to say so, similar to (the first clause of) utensils with which food is not prepared, where it is speaking of [utensils] the likes of which are not rented out, which we establish in Nedarim (32b) in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer:

Tosafot on Megillah 8a:4:1.hebrew: אין בין נדר לנדבה - קשיא, אמאי לא תני שנדבה באה מן המעשר, דכתיב (דברים כ״ז:ז׳) "וזבחת שלמים" גבי מעשר, ונדר אינו בא אלא מן החולין, וכיון דאמר "הרי עלי" הוי נדר? וי"ל, דמן הדין לא תנא ליה, משום דאיירי בקרבן שהופרש כבר, ואשמעינן דאין חילוק בעבודתן; אבל בקרבן שלא הופרש, פשיטא ליה שיש הרבה חילוקים. אי נמי, דתנא ושייר. ונהי ד"אין בין" קאמר, דמשמע דהוי דוקא, כדאמר במרובה (ב"ק דף סב: ושם), מ"מ לא קשיא, דבמסכת תענית (דף יג: ושם) אשכחן "אין בין" דשייר; דקאמר: "אין בין שלש אמצעיות", וכי תימא תנא ושייר, והא "אין בין" קתני! ופריך: ותסברא "אין בין" דווקא? והא שייר תיבה! ומשני: אי משום תיבה, לאו שיורא הוא. מכל מקום משמע, דאי הוה משייר ליה, לא הוה קשיא ליה כלל, אף על גב דקתני "אין בין":
Tosafot on Megillah 8a:4:1.english: There is no [difference] between a vow [offering] and a gift [offering] - It is difficult: why does [the Mishnah] not teach that a gift [offering] may come from tithe [money] — as it is written (Deuteronomy 27:7), "And you shall sacrifice peace-offerings," regarding tithe — whereas a vow [offering] comes only from unconsecrated [funds], since once he says, "It is hereby upon me," it is a vow? And one can answer that by right [the Tanna] did not teach it, because he is dealing with an offering that has already been designated, and he teaches us that there is no difference in their [sacrificial] service; however, regarding an offering that has not yet been designated, it is obvious to him that there are many differences. Alternatively, [one can answer] that [the Tanna] taught [some differences] and left out [others]. And although [the Mishnah] says "There is no [difference] between," which implies that it is exact, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] Merubah (Bava Kamma 62b and [the parallel] there), nevertheless it is not difficult; for in tractate Taanit (13b and [the parallel] there) we find "There is no [difference] between" where [the Tanna] left out [cases]. For [the Gemara] says: "There is no [difference] between the middle three [fasts]" — "And if you say [the Tanna] taught [some] and left out [others], behold it teaches 'There is no [difference] between'!" And [the Gemara] objects: "Now do you think 'There is no [difference] between' is exact? Behold he left out [the matter of] the ark!" And [the Gemara] answers: "If [your objection is] because of the ark, that is not an omission." In any event, it is implied that if [the Tanna] had left [something] out, it would not have been difficult for [the Gemara] at all, even though it teaches "There is no [difference] between":
